title: 2,558 Commits. One $19 Sale.
caption:
Three businesses run by AI agents, in public. Combined revenue: $18.09.

One gave Claude Code a VPS, live accounts and 72 hours to make $1,000. It shipped a 151-page ebook, a $39 code kit, a $149 done-for-you offer and a free MCP server, and made $0. Store: 133 views, 6 orders, all six chose $0 on pay-what-you-want. The other two: $18.09 net on day 19, and 0 euros on day 16.

The part I can't argue with: all three had product before they had a channel. I do that too — I ship, then go looking for someone to show it to. And the one sale that did land came from a free book, a free cover, then a price dialog the buyer never clicked to open.

Where did your last sale come from?

slides.headline:
2,558 Commits.
One $19 Sale.
slides.sub: Three agents, six products, 22 days of building in public. First money landed on day 19: $19, minus Stripe's fee, $18.09 net.

slides.headline:
$1,000 Goal.
72 Hours. $0.
slides.sub: Claude Code got a VPS, live accounts and an old course to resell. It shipped a 151-page ebook, a $39 code kit, a $149 offer and a free MCP server.

slides.title: No Channel Existed
items: Four products shipped before there was one place a human would see them.
X organic: 2–8 impressions a post, on 500 followers that were mostly bots.
A $41 X ad: 16,569 impressions, 70 clicks, nothing sold.
Product Hunt: one upvote, his own. Reddit removed the posts.

slides.headline:
Free Was
The Product
slides.sub: 133 store views, 6 orders, all six chose $0 on pay-what-you-want. A second agent gave the fix away for ten days: six founders thanked it, none paid.

slides.headline:
A Price They
Never Asked For
slides.sub: The one sale: free book, free cover, then a dialog that opens by itself. 26 minutes from a Google search to $19. They never pressed the price button.

slides.headline:
Before You
Ship Again
slides.sub: and I’ll send all three ledgers
